title: Gradual Exposure Concierge — interactive safety net for traffic reassignment
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and prototype a lightweight, guided UI layer that surfaces a live 'safety net' for gradual exposure flows (canary/AB/percentage splits) to let operators reassign, quarantine, or snapshot cohorts without full rollback. Goal: reduce mean time to safe state during rollout anomalies by giving operators a clear one-click reassignment path, contextual signals, and explainable impact estimation before commit.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive prototype (Figma) demonstrates reassignment ribbon and cohort quarantine modal with realistic data and microinteractions
Design handoff doc includes component spec, ARIA/accessibility notes, color tokens, and motion timings
Handoff includes API contract for suggested reassignment percentages, available variants, and telemetry hooks (ENG signoff)
Usability testing with 6 non-design engineers yields net positive understanding and shows operators can complete safe-reassign flow within 45s
Edge cases documented: multi-region deployments, not-enough-capacity fallback, and permission gating
engineering_notes: Core runtime exposure API expected: /v1/rollouts/{id}/reassign POST body {targetVariant, percent, reason} — ENG to confirm schema (see ENG-2345)
Need server-side support for dry-run estimation endpoint: /v1/rollouts/{id}/estimate-reassign to compute expected latency/cost delta
Telemetry: emit rollout.action.reassign events with previous/next split and operator id
Fallback behavior: if variant capacity insufficient, show 'queue for reassignment' state and surface ETA
Security: only users with rollout:modify scope can perform change; design includes a confirmation modal for high-impact (>30%) changes
